top_news.title: OmniPMNet: Bridging discrete and gridded PM10 forecasts via omni-query neural processes
top_news.dek: OmniPM-Net fuses chemical transport models and graph neural networks to improve PM10 air quality forecasting.
top_news.brief: OmniPM-Net uses a Convolutional Conditional Neural Process to reconcile gridded chemical transport model outputs with discrete station-based graph neural network data. By employing a terrain-aware Gaussian set convolution, the model creates a unified spatial representation that improves accuracy for both local monitoring sites and broader regional fields during dust events.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing the fusion of gridded and discrete air quality data points

top_news.title: KV - Deprecate legacy Workers KV namespace API routes
top_news.dek: Cloudflare is deprecating legacy Workers KV API routes, requiring migration to the new storage path by October 15, 2026.
top_news.brief: Legacy API routes under /accounts/{account_id}/workers/namespaces/* are being phased out. Developers must update their integration paths to /accounts/{account_id}/storage/kv/namespaces/ before the October 15 deadline. The new routes are functionally identical to the legacy versions.
top_news.image_alt: Cloudflare Workers KV API migration diagram

top_news.title: OpenAI's Codex now encrypts instructions between AI agents, leaving developers blind to internal delegation
top_news.dek: OpenAI's Codex now encrypts internal agent-to-agent instructions, limiting developer visibility into task delegation.
top_news.brief: Codex has implemented mandatory encryption for internal communications between main agents and subagents. This change prevents developers from auditing how complex tasks are broken down and delegated, particularly within the Sol and Terra model variants.
top_news.image_alt: Abstract representation of encrypted AI agent communication

top_news.title: Google Releases LiteRT.js: A JavaScript Binding of LiteRT That Runs .tflite Models in Browsers via WebGPU
top_news.dek: Google's new LiteRT.js library enables high-performance .tflite model inference in browsers using WebGPU and WebNN.
top_news.brief: LiteRT.js provides a JavaScript binding for on-device inference, utilizing WebAssembly, XNNPACK, and WebGPU. Google claims up to 3x performance gains over existing web runtimes, with significant speedups when leveraging GPU or NPU hardware acceleration.

top_news.title: Show HN: I RL-trained an agent that trains models with RL (for ~$1.3k)
top_news.dek: An open-source project demonstrates an RL-trained agent capable of autonomously training other models via reinforcement learning.
top_news.brief: The project provides a full pipeline for an AI agent to define training jobs, including environment and reward configuration, and execute them on external GPU clusters. All weights, training scripts, and orchestration code are available on GitHub.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram of an RL agent training pipeline

primary.summary: The legacy Workers KV API routes under /accounts/{account_id}/workers/namespaces/* are deprecated as of July 15, 2026, and will stop working on October 15, 2026. Migrate to the documented Workers KV API routes under /accounts/{account_id}/storage/kv/namespaces/* before that date. The legacy and replacement routes are interchangeable. What you need to do Update any integration that calls a route under /accounts/{account_id}/workers/

primary.summary: Google released LiteRT.js on July 9, 2026. It is a JavaScript binding of LiteRT, Google's on-device inference library. The runtime executes .tflite models directly in the browser through WebAssembly, with XNNPACK on CPU, ML Drift over WebGPU, and experimental WebNN for NPUs. Google reports up to 3x gains over other web runtimes, and 5–60x for GPU or NPU over its own CPU path. One detail the announcement omits: tensors are manually managed and must be deleted.
